data.long_meaning: A state of peace, inner calmness and tranquility. data.cultural_impact: The name "Shanti" is common among Hindus and is often used as a personal name or a title for respect. It carries a rich cultural significance and is believed to bestow peace and serenity not just upon the bearer of the name but also around them. In Hindu society, "Shanti" is often invoked during religious rituals and ceremonies to request for peace and harmony within the family, community or the surroundings. It is also a popular greeting and farewell amongst Hindus, reflecting the importance of peace and calmness in daily life.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, "Shanti" holds a deep spiritual significance as it represents the attainment of inner peace and tranquility. It is a state of mind that is untouched by external circumstances and is completely serene. Achieving the state of "Shanti" is considered as a pinnacle of spiritual development, as it helps an individual to attain the ultimate peace and self-realization. Thus, the name "Shanti" serves as a constant reminder to always strive towards maintaining inner peace and calmness, and to deal with the vicissitudes of life with equanimity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shanti is a Sanskrit word meaning peace, serenity, and tranquility. It is a name that invokes the blessings of the peaceful Goddess Saraswati and the calming influence of the eternal river Ganga. May one named Shanti be ever bathed in inner peace and radiate the same to all around.

vedic_reference.note: Shanti is a popular name in Hindu mythology and is often used as a name for the goddess of peace and tranquility. It is also used as a name for the wife of the god Shiva in Hindu mythology.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Shanti was a popular name for women in ancient India. The name Shanti carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Shanti is a Sanskrit name meaning peace, tranquility, and calmness.

trends: Shanti is a common name for girls in India
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Shanti remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: Devi Shanti, a teacher in Chennai, India, shares that their name Shanti meaning "Peace, Calmness" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
